chapters.title: Alas for the Day!
chapters.html:
Joel 1

What the Locust Left

1The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.

2Hear this, you elders;
give ear, all inhabitants of the land!
Has such a thing happened in your days,
or in the days of your fathers?

3Tell your children of it,
and let your children tell their children,
and their children another generation.

4What the cutting locust left,
the locust has eaten;
what the locust left,
the young locust has eaten;
and what the young locust left,
the grasshopper has eaten.

Wake Up and Weep

5Wake up, you drunkards, and weep;
wail, all you drinkers of wine,
over the sweet wine,
for it is cut off from your mouth.

6For a nation has come up against my land,
mighty and without number;
its teeth are the teeth of a lion,
and it has the jaws of a lioness.

7It has made my vine a waste
and my fig tree splinters;
it has utterly stripped it bare and thrown it down;
its tendrils have turned white.

8Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth
for the husband of her youth.

9Grain offering and drink offering are cut off
from the house of the LORD;
the priests mourn,
the ministers of the LORD.

10The field is devastated,
the ground mourns;
for the grain is devastated,
the new wine dries up,
the oil wastes away.

11Be ashamed, you farmers;
wail, you vinedressers,
over the wheat and over the barley,
for the harvest of the field has perished.

12The vine dries up,
and the fig tree wastes away;
pomegranate, palm too, and apple tree,
all the trees of the field are dried up;
for joy has dried up
from the sons of men.

Proclaim a Solemn Assembly

13Gird yourselves and lament, you priests;
wail, you ministers of the altar;
come, spend the night in sackcloth,
you ministers of my God;
for grain offering and drink offering are withheld
from the house of your God.

14Consecrate a fast;
proclaim a solemn assembly;
gather the elders,
all the inhabitants of the land,
to the house of the LORD your God,
and cry out to the LORD.

The Day of the LORD Is Near

15Alas for the day!
For the day of the LORD is near,
and it will come like destruction from the Almighty.

16Is not the food cut off
before our eyes,
joy and gladness
from the house of our God?

17The seeds shrivel under their clods;
the storehouses are desolate;
the granaries are torn down,
for the grain has dried up.

18How the beasts groan!
The herds of cattle wander in confusion,
because they have no pasture;
even the flocks of sheep bear the guilt.

19To You, LORD, I call,
for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness,
and flame has burned up all the trees of the field.

20Even the beasts of the field long for You,
for the streams of water are dried up,
and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.

Notes

  • v1 "The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel" — Joel names no king and no year, where Hosea and Amos name both (Hosea 1:1; Amos 1:1). Yo'el, Joel, is also the name of Samuel's firstborn (1 Samuel 8:2). For Pethuel the Greek has Bathouel, the Greek spelling of Bethuel, Rebekah's father (Genesis 24:15).

  • vv2–3 "Has such a thing happened in your days… Tell your children of it" — the words of the locusts of Egypt: such as your fathers and your fathers' fathers have not seen (Exodus 10:6), and Before them there had never been locusts like them (Exodus 10:14). The telling down the generations is the charge given with that plague, so that you may tell in the ears of your son and your son's son what I did in Egypt (Exodus 10:2): there the plague fell on Egypt; here it falls on the land of the house of the LORD (v9).

  • v4 "the cutting locust… the locust… the young locust… the grasshopper" — four names: gazam, arbeh, yeleq, chasil. Arbeh, locust, is the locust of Egypt (Exodus 10:14); gazam is the one that in Amos devoured your many gardens and vineyards (Amos 4:9); yeleq is in the locusts came, young locusts without number (Psalm 105:34); and chasil in locust or grasshopper (1 Kings 8:37), from the verb of for the locust will consume it (Deuteronomy 28:38). Yeter, what… left, is the word of the locusts of Egypt, which will eat what is left of what escaped (Exodus 10:5). Whether they are four kinds or four waves, the verse does not say; the LORD names all four again in 2:25. The Greek has caterpillar, locust, wingless locust, blight.

  • vv5–7 "Wake up, you drunkards… a nation has come up against my land… its teeth are the teeth of a lion" — the drunkards are called first, to weep for the wine. The locusts are called goy, a nation, an army without number, with the teeth of Judah's lion in Jacob's blessing, like a lion, and like a lioness (Genesis 49:9); metalle'ot, jaws, is the word of I broke the jaws of the unjust (Job 29:17). The vine and the fig tree are the sign of peace, each man under his vine and under his fig tree (Micah 4:4), and what Hosea foretold, I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees (Hosea 2:12). Chasof chasafah, utterly stripped it bare, and the sarigim, tendrils, as on the vine of the cupbearer's dream (Genesis 40:10), are left white.

  • v8 "Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth" — eli, lament, is said to a woman, the land; its letters spell elai, to me, and the Greek has Lament to me. A betulah, virgin, mourning the husband of her youth may be a young woman mourning the man she was promised to, for the law calls a betrothed virgin his neighbor's wife (Deuteronomy 22:24).

  • vv9, 13 "Grain offering and drink offering are cut off… spend the night in sackcloth" — with no grain and no wine, the daily offering stops: a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine, for the one lamb, morning and evening (Exodus 29:40–41). Meshartei YHWH, the ministers of the LORD, are the priests at the altar. They are to lie the night in sackcloth, as Ahab lay in sackcloth when he heard the word against him (1 Kings 21:27).

  • vv10–12 "the new wine dries up… Be ashamed, you farmers… joy has dried up" — the grain, new wine and oil are the blessing of the law, your grain and your new wine and your oil (Deuteronomy 7:13), which Israel did not know were the LORD's gift, She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine and the oil (Hosea 2:8). Hovish, said five times in this chapter (vv10, 11, 12 twice, 17), is a form of two verbs, yavesh, dry up, and bosh, be ashamed: the wine dries up, the farmers are put to shame, and joy does both. Shuddad sadeh, the field is devastated, the two words nearly alike. Umlal, wastes away, is Hosea's all who live in it waste away (Hosea 4:3).

  • v14 "Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly" — qir'u atsarah are the words of Jehu's trap, Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal (2 Kings 10:20); here it is for the LORD, and the whole land is called in with the elders. The call is given again in 2:15–16.

  • v15 "Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near" — ahah la-yom, as Ezekiel was told to cry over Egypt, Wail, 'Alas for the day!' For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near (Ezekiel 30:2–3). The rest is word for word Isaiah's against Babylon, Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; it will come like destruction from the Almighty (Isaiah 13:6), and the English follows his. Shod mi-Shaddai, destruction from the Almighty, plays on the name of God Almighty (Genesis 17:1). Amos had warned, Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD! (Amos 5:18).

  • vv17–20 "The seeds shrivel… even the flocks of sheep bear the guilt… the beasts of the field long for You" — v17 is obscure: avshu, shrivel, megrefot, clods, and mammegurot, granaries, are found only here; the Greek has the heifers leaped at their mangers. Navokhu, wander in confusion, is what Pharaoh said of Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 14:3). Ne'shamu, bear the guilt, is the verb of now they must bear their guilt (Hosea 10:2): the flocks suffer for the guilt of men. The Greek has were destroyed, as if from nashammu, are desolate (v17), nearly the same letters. Ta'arog, long for, is the deer of As a deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for You, God (Psalm 42:1), with the same afiqei mayim, streams of water: the beasts pray as the prophet prays (v19).

chapters.title: I Will Pour Out My Spirit
chapters.html:
Joel 2

The LORD's Army

1Blow the horn in Zion;
sound the alarm on My holy mountain!
Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble,
for the day of the LORD is coming;
it is near —

2a day of darkness and gloom,
a day of cloud and thick darkness!
Like dawn spread out over the mountains
comes a people great and mighty;
there has never been the like of it from of old,
nor will there be again after it,
through the years of generation after generation.

3Before it fire devours,
and behind it a flame burns;
the land before it is like the garden of Eden,
and behind it a desolate wilderness,
and no one escapes it.

4Its appearance is like the appearance of horses,
and like horsemen, so they run.

5As with the noise of chariots
they skip on the tops of the mountains,
like the noise of a flame of fire
devouring stubble,
like a mighty people
drawn up for battle.

6Before it peoples writhe;
all faces grow pale.

7Like warriors they run;
like men of war they climb the wall;
they march each on his way,
and they do not swerve from their paths.

8They do not jostle one another;
each marches in his track;
they plunge through the weapons
and are not cut off.

9They leap on the city;
they run on the wall;
they climb into the houses;
they enter through the windows like a thief.

10Before it the earth trembles,
the heavens shake;
the sun and the moon grow dark,
and the stars withdraw their shining.

11The LORD utters His voice
before His army,
for His camp is very great;
for mighty is the one who does His word.
For the day of the LORD is great
and very fearful;
who can endure it?

Return to Me

12Yet even now, declares the LORD,
return to Me with all your heart,
with fasting, with weeping and with lamenting.

13Tear your hearts and not your garments,
and return to the LORD your God;
for He is gracious and merciful,
slow to anger and abundant in loyal love,
and He relents of disaster.

14Who knows? He may turn and relent,
and leave a blessing behind Him,
a grain offering and a drink offering
for the LORD your God.

15Blow the horn in Zion;
consecrate a fast;
proclaim a solemn assembly;

16gather the people;
consecrate the assembly;
bring together the elders;
gather the children
and those who nurse at the breast;
let the bridegroom go out of his room,
and the bride out of her chamber.

17Between the porch and the altar
let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep,
and let them say,
"Spare Your people, LORD,
and do not give Your inheritance to scorn,
for the nations to rule over them.
Why should they say among the peoples,
'Where is their God?'"

The LORD Answers

18Then the LORD was jealous for His land
and had pity on His people.

19The LORD answered and said to His people:
I am about to send you
the grain, the new wine and the oil,
and you will be satisfied with it;
and I will no longer make you
a scorn among the nations.

20The northerner I will remove far from you,
and drive him into a land dry and desolate,
his front into the eastern sea
and his rear into the western sea;
his stench will go up,
and his foul smell will rise,
for he has done great things.

21Do not fear, O ground;
rejoice and be glad,
for the LORD has done great things!

22Do not fear, you beasts of the field,
for the pastures of the wilderness are green;
for the tree bears its fruit;
the fig tree and the vine
give their full strength.

23You sons of Zion,
rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God,
for He has given you the early rain for righteousness;
He has brought down rain for you,
the early rain and the late rain, at the first.

24The threshing floors will be full of grain,
and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

25I will repay you for the years
that the locust has eaten,
the young locust, the grasshopper and the cutting locust,
My great army,
which I sent among you.

26You will surely eat and be satisfied,
and praise the name of the LORD your God,
who has dealt wondrously with you;
and My people will never be put to shame.

27You will know that I am among Israel,
and that I am the LORD your God,
and there is no other;
and My people will never be put to shame.

I Will Pour Out My Spirit

28And it shall come to pass afterward
that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh;
your sons and your daughters will prophesy,
your old men will dream dreams,
and your young men will see visions.

29Even on the male servants and the female servants
in those days I will pour out My Spirit.

30I will give wonders
in the heavens and on the earth:
blood and fire and columns of smoke.

31The sun will be turned to darkness,
and the moon to blood,
before the great and fearful day of the LORD comes.

32And it shall come to pass
that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape;
for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem
there will be those who escape,
as the LORD has said,
and among the survivors
those whom the LORD calls.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Blow the horn in Zion… a day of darkness and gloom… no one escapes it" — the alarm of Hosea, Blow the horn in Gibeah… Sound the alarm (Hosea 5:8), now on Zion itself. The day is Amos's darkness, and not light, gloom with no brightness in it (Amos 5:20), and the cloud of Sinai, darkness, cloud and thick darkness (Deuteronomy 4:11). There has never been the like of it is said of the locusts of Egypt, Before them there had never been locusts like them, and after them there will not be (Exodus 10:14). The garden before and the wilderness behind is the promise run backward, This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden (Ezekiel 36:35). Peletah, escape, is what the locusts of Egypt ate up, what is left of what escaped (Exodus 10:5), and the word comes back in v32.

  • vv4–9 "like horsemen, so they run… all faces grow pale… they enter through the windows like a thief" — the army may be the locusts of chapter 1 seen as soldiers, or soldiers seen as locusts; the chapter names it only His army (v11) and, in v25, My great army, with the four locust names. Kibbetsu pa'rur, grow pale, is uncertain, word for word gather pa'rur, perhaps a glow; the phrase is found again only in Nahum, of Nineveh. The Greek has every face like a scorched pot: parur, pot, has nearly the same letters, the word of boiled it in pots (Numbers 11:8). Yashoqqu, they leap, is the verb of as locusts leap, men leap on it (Isaiah 33:4). Houses full of them were the word to Pharaoh, Your houses will be full (Exodus 10:6).

  • vv10–11 "the earth trembles, the heavens shake… The LORD utters His voice before His army… who can endure it?" — the lights fail as on Babylon's day, the sun will be dark at its rising, and the moon will not shine its light (Isaiah 13:10). Natan qolo, utters His voice, is the LORD's roar from Zion in Amos 1:2. Machanehu, His camp, is the word of Jacob's This is God's camp (Genesis 32:2), and the one who does His word is said of His messengers, mighty in strength, who do His word (Psalm 103:20). Mi yekhilennu, who can endure it, as in the nations cannot endure His indignation (Jeremiah 10:10).

  • vv12–14 "Yet even now… return to Me… Tear your hearts and not your garments… Who knows?" — shuvu adai, return to Me, answers Amos's refrain, yet you did not return to Me, declares the LORD (Amos 4:6), said of the locust too (Amos 4:9); with all your heart is the law's, when you return to the LORD your God with all your heart (Deuteronomy 30:10). To tear the garments is the outward sign, as Ahab tore his clothes (1 Kings 21:27). The name is the LORD's own from Sinai, God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love (Exodus 34:6), with gracious put first, and Jonah says it again in the same order (Jonah 4:2). He relents of disaster, as the LORD relented of the evil at the calf (Exodus 32:14). Who knows? is David's word as he fasted, Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me (2 Samuel 12:22). The blessing left behind is the grain offering and drink offering that were cut off (1:9, 13).

  • vv15–17 "let the bridegroom go out of his room… Between the porch and the altar… Where is their God?" — no one is excused: not the infants, not the bridegroom, whom the law sends home for a year, he shall not go out with the army (Deuteronomy 24:5). Chuppah, the bride's chamber, is the word of like a bridegroom from his chamber (Psalm 19:5). Between the porch and the altar is where Ezekiel saw twenty-five men bow to the sun (Ezekiel 8:16); here the priests weep there. Li-mshol bam goyim, for the nations to rule over them, can also be read for the nations to make a proverb of them, from mashal, the proverb of a horror, a proverb and a byword (Deuteronomy 28:37); the Greek has to rule over them. The last line is word for word the psalm's but for among the peoples: Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" (Psalm 79:10).

  • vv18–20 "Then the LORD was jealous for His land… The northerner I will remove far from you… for he has done great things" — va-yeqanne, was jealous, is the LORD of the commandment, a jealous God (Exodus 20:5), jealous now for His land. Hineni sholeach, I am about to send, gives back the grain, new wine and oil of 1:10. Ha-tsefoni, the northerner, is the enemy out of the north of Jeremiah, Out of the north disaster will break loose (Jeremiah 1:14). The eastern sea (Ezekiel 47:18) and the western sea (Deuteronomy 11:24) are the land's two borders, east and west. The stench is the plague of frogs, the land stank (Exodus 8:14). Ki higdil la'asot, for he has done great things, ends v20 of the enemy and v21 of the LORD: the pride of the one is answered by the deeds of the other, The LORD has done great things for us (Psalm 126:3).

  • vv21–24 "Do not fear, O ground… the pastures of the wilderness are green… the early rain for righteousness" — chapter 1 is undone in its own words: the ground that mourned (1:10), the beasts that longed for God (1:20), the pastures the fire devoured (1:19), the fig tree and the vine (1:7, 12). Cheilam, their full strength, is chayil, the word for His army (v11): the vine gives its strength where the army took it. Ha-moreh li-tsdaqah is the early rain for righteousness, as moreh is the early rain in Psalm 84:6 and in this verse's next line; moreh is also teacher, your eyes will see your Teacher (Isaiah 30:20), and the verb is Hosea's until He comes and rains righteousness on you (Hosea 10:12). The Greek has the food for righteousness. The early rain and the late rain are the law's promise (Deuteronomy 11:14); ba-rishon, at the first, is in the first month, or as before, and the Greek has as before.

  • vv25–27 "I will repay you for the years… My great army… My people will never be put to shame" — ve-shillamti, I will repay, is the verb of Hosea's the days of repayment (Hosea 9:7), now turned to Israel's good. The four of 1:4 come back in another order, and are named the LORD's own great army, which I sent among you. Akhol ve-savoa, surely eat and be satisfied, is the law's You will eat and be satisfied (Deuteronomy 8:10), where the curse had said you will eat and not be satisfied (Leviticus 26:26). Lo yevoshu, will never be put to shame, twice, is bosh, the verb of the farmers' shame (1:11). Be-qerev Yisra'el ani, I am among Israel, answers the false boast of Micah's rulers, Is not the LORD among us? (Micah 3:11), with the LORD's own word; and there is no other is His word in Isaiah, I am the LORD, and there is no other (Isaiah 45:5).

  • vv28–29 "I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh… Even on the male servants and the female servants" — in the Hebrew text vv28–32 are 3:1–5, and chapter 3 is chapter 4; the English numbering is followed. Ve-hayah acharei khen, and it shall come to pass afterward: after the rain, the Spirit. Moses had wished it, If only all the LORD's people were prophets, and the LORD would put His Spirit on them! (Numbers 11:29), and Ezekiel and Isaiah heard it promised, when I have poured out My Spirit on the house of Israel (Ezekiel 39:29), I will pour My Spirit on your seed (Isaiah 44:3). The Spirit falls on old and young, sons and daughters, and the lowest of the house, male servants and female servants, the pair of Genesis 12:16. The Greek has of My Spirit and My servants, and Peter follows it at Pentecost as far as will escape in v32, with in the last days for afterward (Acts 2:16–21).

  • vv30–32 "blood and fire and columns of smoke… everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape" — mofetim, wonders, are the signs and wonders the LORD gave against Egypt (Deuteronomy 6:22), and the smoke is Sinai's, Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln (Exodus 19:18); columns of smoke is the phrase of Song of Songs 3:6. The sun and moon darkened in v10 are now turned to darkness and to blood, and the great and fearful day is v11's. Calling on the name of the LORD is as old as Seth's son, Then it was begun, calling on the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26). Yimmalet, will escape, and peletah, those who escape: none escaped the army (v3), and some will escape the day, as Isaiah heard, out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion (Isaiah 37:32). Yiqra, calls on, and qore, calls: those who call on the LORD are those the LORD calls. The Greek has those who bring good news, whom the Lord has called.

speech.text: Joel 2
The LORD's Army
Blow the horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming; it is near —

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness! Like dawn spread out over the mountains comes a people great and mighty; there has never been the like of it from of old, nor will there be again after it, through the years of generation after generation.
Before it fire devours, and behind it a flame burns; the land before it is like the garden of Eden, and behind it a desolate wilderness, and no one escapes it.
Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like horsemen, so they run.
As with the noise of chariots they skip on the tops of the mountains, like the noise of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Before it peoples writhe; all faces grow pale.
Like warriors they run; like men of war they climb the wall; they march each on his way, and they do not swerve from their paths.
They do not jostle one another; each marches in his track; they plunge through the weapons and are not cut off.
They leap on the city; they run on the wall; they climb into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.
Before it the earth trembles, the heavens shake; the sun and the moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their shining.
The LORD utters His voice before His army, for His camp is very great; for mighty is the one who does His word. For the day of the LORD is great and very fearful; who can endure it?
Return to Me
Yet even now, declares the LORD, return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping and with lamenting.
Tear your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God; for He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loyal love, and He relents of disaster.
Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind Him, a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
Blow the horn in Zion; consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly;
gather the people; consecrate the assembly; bring together the elders; gather the children and those who nurse at the breast; let the bridegroom go out of his room, and the bride out of her chamber.

Between the porch and the altar let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep, and let them say, "Spare Your people, LORD, and do not give Your inheritance to scorn, for the nations to rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
The LORD Answers
Then the LORD was jealous for His land and had pity on His people.
The LORD answered and said to His people: I am about to send you the grain, the new wine and the oil, and you will be satisfied with it; and I will no longer make you a scorn among the nations.

The northerner I will remove far from you, and drive him into a land dry and desolate, his front into the eastern sea and his rear into the western sea; his stench will go up, and his foul smell will rise, for he has done great things.
Do not fear, O ground; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things!
Do not fear, you beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness are green; for the tree bears its fruit; the fig tree and the vine give their full strength.
You sons of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God, for He has given you the early rain for righteousness; He has brought down rain for you, the early rain and the late rain, at the first.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years that the locust has eaten, the young locust, the grasshopper and the cutting locust, My great army, which I sent among you.
You will surely eat and be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and My people will never be put to shame.
You will know that I am among Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other; and My people will never be put to shame.
I Will Pour Out My Spirit
And it shall come to pass afterward that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on the male servants and the female servants in those days I will pour out My Spirit.
I will give wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the great and fearful day of the LORD comes.

And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said, and among the survivors those whom the LORD calls.
